command:
set +e
set -uo pipefail
export TMPDIR=/tmp HOME=/tmp
cd /tmp

# spawn runs task commands under bash -e; `set -uo pipefail` does not clear it (spawn#707).
# No PATH export: aarchsci env images already have their python first.

echo "== staged bytes must match their pins =="
sha256sum -c pins.sha256 || { echo "FAIL: model.py does not match its pin"; exit 1; }

echo "== versions, read from the running binaries rather than the env lock =="
# A lock file in git and an image in a registry are two different artifacts.
mf6 -v 2>&1 | grep -oE 'mf6: [0-9.]+' | sed 's/^/  /'
python3 -u -c "
import flopy, numpy
print('  flopy        %s' % getattr(flopy, '__version__', 'unknown'))
print('  numpy        %s' % getattr(numpy, '__version__', 'unknown'))
" || { echo "FAIL: flopy does not import"; exit 1; }
command -v mf6 >/dev/null || { echo "FAIL: mf6 absent from this image"; exit 1; }

# python3 -u so a killed run still has its output in command.log.
python3 -u model.py 2>&1 | tee identities.log
RC="${PIPESTATUS[0]}"

# Copy the solver's OWN listings out BEFORE acting on the exit code: a first version did this
# after the check, so the one run that failed staged no listing at all -- exactly the evidence
# needed to diagnose it. spawn never uploads a tool's log unless the spec declares it an output.
cp case1/m.lst mf6-case1.lst 2>/dev/null
cp case2_201/m.lst mf6-case2-finest.lst 2>/dev/null
cp score.tsv modflow-diag.txt 2>/dev/null
test "$RC" = "0" || { echo "FAIL: an identity failed"; exit 1; }
uname -m | awk '{print "arch\t"$1}'
echo "DONE"
